answers.core: This is the common use case/expected behavior, really.  I'd say it should just behave in the way that's intuitive out of the box.
answers.workaround:
It can be worked around, but it took an experienced dev several days, multiple forum posts, discussions on discord, and help from twitch chat to figure out how to do it.

This is ultimately what I ended up with:

```
func _ready():
	get_viewport().connect("size_changed", self, "_on_viewport_size_changed")
	UpdateUIViewports()


func _on_viewport_size_changed():
	UpdateUIViewports()


func UpdateUIViewports():
	var TheFinalTransform := get_viewport().get_final_transform()
	var RootViewportSize := get_viewport().size
	var RectScale := Vector2(TheFinalTransform.x.x, TheFinalTransform.y.y)
	var InvRectScale := Vector2.ONE / RectScale
	ViewportUI.size = RootViewportSize
	ViewportContainerUI.rect_scale = InvRectScale
	ViewportUI.get_child(0).rect_scale = RectScale
	# This part isn't as critical, but I have another viewport acting as an accumulation buffer for a glow effect:
	ViewportUIGlow.size = RootViewportSize
	ViewportContainerGlow.rect_scale = InvRectScale
	ViewportUIGlow.set_clear_mode(Viewport.CLEAR_MODE_ONLY_NEXT_FRAME)
```

Not a lot of code, but it took a while to figure out + a lot of finagling with the controls on the menu to make sure they were positioned correctly within the viewport.

title: Add an option to automatically scale viewport resolution to match window resolution
